title: Understanding 64-bit Support in 4D v12
author: Josh Fletcher, Technical Services Team Member, 4D Inc.
featured_technology: 4D Server v12 x64 (Windows-only, beta at v12 launch)
64-bit memory addressing and larger server cache

historical_commentary.text: This note pre-announced 4D Server v12's first 64-bit executable (Windows-only, still in beta at v12's release) and carefully managed expectations that 64-bit support is chiefly about breaking the ~4GB memory ceiling for larger caches and more concurrent clients, not a general performance "magic bullet." 64-bit 4D Server is now the sole, standard deployment target across Mac and Windows — 32-bit 4D Server has long since been discontinued — so the note's forward-looking explanation of why 64-bit matters (larger cache, more clients) remains conceptually accurate, but its framing of 64-bit as a new/optional/beta feature and Windows-only limitation is entirely obsolete history.
related_updates: 4D Server has been 64-bit-only (Mac and Windows) for many years; 32-bit 4D Server was fully discontinued
Current 4D documentation on server sizing/cache configuration supersedes this note's forward-looking, beta-era guidance
